newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht, interbank rate steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht, interbank rate steady in late trade.

text.p: The Thai baht held steady in late Wednesday trade as tightened baht supply and high short-term Thai interest rates curbed demand for dollar, dealers said.
"Dollar buying eased relatively today because short-term Thai interest rates are very high," said a dealer at a major Thai bank.

Another dealer at a European bank said moderate dollar buying in the afternoon was not as strong as in the past few days. "(Dollar) buying side was very thin today. They may fear possible central bank intervention," the dealer said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate unchanged from Tuesday at 25.55.
The overnight interbank rate was largely steady at 14.75-15.00 percent in late trade against 14.50-15.00 in the morning, dealers said.
Dealers said money supply remained tight following heavy dollar buying in the currency market and ahead of a deadline for commercial banks to meet central bank reserve requirement later this week.
"The market continued seeing strong borrowings. Some fund injection through the central bank's bond repurchase window slowed the rise in interbank rates," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was quoted at 11.00/12.00 satangs per dollar on late Wednesday against 10.50/11.25 in the morning.
